system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager

T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior infrastructure engineer with 10 years of experience, including six running Kubernetes platforms
on AWS. Technical lead with hands-on experience in cloud infrastructure design and operation,
Terraform, developer self-service, observability and incident management. Delivered platforms
adopted by 14 product teams, reduced service deployment lead time from approximately two weeks to
under one day, and cut EC2 costs by 38%.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS, EKS, EC2, ECS, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53,
CloudFront, Linux
Infrastructure as code and delivery: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Argo CD, Helm,
Kustomize, GitHub Actions, Puppet
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, Loki, OpenTelemetry, Sloth,
PagerDuty, SLOs, error budgets, incident management, k6
Engineering: Go, Python, Bash, Kubernetes controllers, system design, capacity planning
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd
Apr 2022 - present
• Technical lead of a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform spanning eight
clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD
ApplicationSets and Crossplane compositions for self-service RDS, SQS and S3 provisioning
through pull requests.
• Enabled all 14 product teams to use the platform; reduced time from new service to production
from approximately two weeks to under one day.
• Introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for the 20 most critical services using Prometheus and Sloth;
agreed an error budget policy with product leadership and reduced weekly on-call pages by
approximately 60%.
• Replaced cluster-autoscaler node groups with Karpenter and Spot instances for stateless workloads,
including interruption handling; reduced EC2 spend by 38%, approximately GBP 410,000 annually.
• Served in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident and post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
• Operated AWS game backend infrastructure across EC2, ECS and EKS for titles with up to 1.2
million daily active players.
• Managed all AWS infrastructure through Terraform, with approximately 40 modules and Atlantis
plan/apply workflows on pull requests.
• Replaced Nagios with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
• Led capacity planning for two major launches; used k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players and
identified and fixed a connection pool limit before launch.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration
management.
• Automated operations with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.
OPEN SOURCE AND TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP
• Built an open-source Kubernetes controller in Go using controller-runtime to delete expired
preview namespaces; approximately 120 GitHub stars.
• Mentored three backend engineers into SRE roles.
• Presented “SLOs that product managers care about” at a UK DevOps meetup in 2024.
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) - 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional - 2023
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
LANGUAGES
English: native | Urdu: conversational

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
Dear Corvale Mobility hiring team,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor - Fleet Connectivity
engagement. Your brief combines cloud infrastructure design with responsibility for taking
systems into production and keeping them observable and reliable. That is the core of my
work: ten years in infrastructure, including six running Kubernetes platforms on AWS, with a
focus on making the safe operational path the easy one for backend developers.
At Tallybrook, I am the technical lead of a five-person platform team operating eight EKS
clusters across three regions for approximately 350 services. I built an internal developer
platform with service templates, Argo CD and Crossplane-based self-service infrastructure,
adopted by all 14 product teams. It reduced the time from a new service to production from
approximately two weeks to under one day. At Brightwater Games, I managed AWS
infrastructure through approximately 40 Terraform modules and Atlantis pull-request
workflows. This is directly relevant to maintaining an approachable infrastructure-as-code
repository and supporting developers in deploying services that are easy to run.
My reliability work combines technical implementation with agreement on how systems should
operate. At Tallybrook, I introduced SLOs and burn-rate alerts for 20 critical services, agreed
an error budget policy with product leadership and reduced weekly on-call pages by
approximately 60%. At Brightwater, I led capacity planning for two major launches; load tests
simulating 300,000 concurrent players exposed a connection pool limit that we fixed before
launch. These experiences provide a practical foundation for contributing to system design
and challenging decisions with evidence.
Corvale’s fleet connectivity scope spans telemetry ingestion, alerting, video streaming and
remote content updates. I would bring proven AWS operations, Terraform, Linux and
technical leadership to the cloud platform supporting those services. I would welcome a
discussion about how that experience could contribute as you shape the architecture and take
it to production.
Best wishes,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
